layers.name: Land outlines
layers.source: OpenStreetMap land polygons, packaged by geo-maps (earth-lands-100m v0.6.0)
layers.processing: Clipped to the strait (simplified to ~600 m) with high-detail boxes for Kinmen, Matsu and Penghu (~20 m) cut out of it so they never overlap; inland lakes removed; coastlines exclude clipping edges; tools/build_land.py.
layers.limitations: 2017 snapshot at 100 m resolution. Land reclaimed since 2017, notably around Xiamen, is not shown.

layers.name: Study areas (Kinmen, Matsu, Penghu)
layers.source: Defined by the author for this project
layers.limitations: Not an official boundary. It includes Xiamen's port approaches, so Xiamen traffic will dominate unsplit counts.

layers.name: Strait median line
layers.source: Taiwan Ministry of National Defense, statement of 2019 (matching its 2004 statement), as reported by Taiwan News
layers.processing: Straight line between the two published endpoints, 27°N 122°E and 23°N 118°E.
layers.limitations: Contested. Beijing has never recognised the line and its foreign ministry denied it exists in 2020.

layers.name: Taiwan baselines, territorial sea and contiguous zone
layers.source: Executive Yuan notice 台88內字第06161號 (10 Feb 1999), amended 院臺建字第0980097355號 (18 Nov 2009): first batch of territorial sea baselines
layers.processing: 22 Taiwan and Penghu base points and 4 Dongsha points (WGS-84) transcribed from the notice; baselines joined in order; 12 and 24 nm buffers in an azimuthal equidistant projection; tools/build_baselines.py. Mainland points checked against the coast (all within ~1 km).
layers.limitations: The short normal-baseline segment at Pengjia Islet (T3–T4) is drawn as a straight line. Diaoyutai and the Spratly baselines are not drawn. Kinmen and Matsu have no baselines in this notice.

layers.name: Submarine cables
layers.source: OpenStreetMap, via an Overpass query exported 22 Nov 2026
layers.processing: Ways tagged as submarine communication or power cables in 21–28°N, 116–123°E; simplified to about 50 m.
layers.limitations: Volunteer-mapped and incomplete: only 14 cable segments, several unnamed; the Taiwan–Matsu cables are absent and TK-2 is mapped only near Kinmen. TeleGeography's fuller dataset requires a licence.

layers.name: Taiwan ADIZ
layers.source: Aeronautical Information Publication, Taipei FIR, ENR 1.12-1, AMDT 02/20 (7 May 2020), Civil Aeronautics Administration
layers.processing: Polygon through the five published vertices: 21°N 117°30′E, 21°N 121°30′E, 22°30′N 123°E, 29°N 123°E, 29°N 117°30′E.
layers.limitations: Copy of the AIP page hosted by a third party (OPSGROUP); check against the current eAIP. An ADIZ is an air-identification procedure, not a claim of sovereign airspace. Some commentary wrongly says its western edge follows the median line.

layers.name: Depth bands
layers.processing: Bands clipped to 112–128°E, 18–31°N and simplified to about 1 km; tools/build_bathymetry.py.
layers.limitations: Small-scale data: it shows the shelf edge but not depth variation inside the strait (e.g. the Taiwan Banks). GEBCO would add that detail.

layers.name: Kinmen prohibited and restricted waters
layers.source: Mainland Affairs Council map of Kinmen restricted and prohibited waters, drawn from MND notice 猛獅字第0930001493號 (7 June 2004, in force 15 June 2004)
layers.processing: 27 corner coordinates read from the official map at 400 dpi and cross-checked against their plotted positions (all within a few hundred metres). Point 2's label is clipped; its seconds are a midpoint estimate (±150 m).
layers.limitations: Digitised from a scanned 2010 PDF of the map. The legal text defines the zones as distances from the low-water line; the map's corner points are the official rendering of that text.

layers.name: Equidistance lines, Kinmen and Matsu (computed)
layers.source: Computed by the author from the land outlines, following the UNCLOS Article 15 default for opposite coasts under 24 nm apart
layers.processing: Kinmen: coast of land touching the official zones, plus Erdan Island from its published coordinates. Matsu: islands near the archipelago's main islands (Wikipedia coordinates for Nangan, Beigan, Juguang, Dongyin, Liang), against the surrounding mainland coast. Coasts sampled every 150 m; boundary between Voronoi regions; tools/build_zones.py.
layers.limitations: Indicative only: 2017 OSM coasts, not surveyed low-water lines; low-tide elevations, China's straight baselines and small islets such as Beiding are not included.

layers.name: Key infrastructure
layers.source: Coordinates from each site's Wikipedia infobox (linked per site)
layers.processing: Only sites with a published coordinate are plotted: 7 around Kinmen, 3 in Matsu, 4 in Penghu.
layers.limitations: Wikipedia coordinates are secondary; Xiang'an airport's failed a cross-check and is excluded. Sources differ on troop presence on Dadan. No PLA installations plotted.

layers.name: International law notes
layers.source: AMTI/CSIS (Sato, 6 Dec 2024); Taipei Times (24 Nov 2009); Global Times (Dec 2025); UNCLOS Arts. 3, 5 and 15
layers.limitations: Taiwan's baseline status is reported as of 2009; check for later changes.

layers.name: Cable incidents (Matsu 2023, Penghu 2025)
layers.source: The Diplomat (April 2023) on the Matsu cables; CNA via GlobalSecurity (12 June 2025) on the Hong Tai 58 case
layers.limitations: Incident locations are described in the sources, not given as coordinates, so they are not plotted.

layers.name: Military balance (Balance tab)
layers.source: US DoD 2022 report (Appendix I) for force counts; DoD 2024 report and IISS Military Balance 2024 for personnel, reserves and coast guards; Defense News (Mar 2026) and CNA (Aug 2025) for 2026 budgets
layers.processing: 18 metrics in data/military.json, each with source, year, definition and caveat; 'facing Taiwan' uses the Eastern and Southern Theaters where the DoD gives them.
layers.limitations: Force counts date from 2022: the 2024 and 2025 DoD reports could not be retrieved, and Chinese numbers have grown since (e.g. a third carrier). Definitions differ between sources; no figure is estimated or interpolated.
